title: AES-256-GCM File Vault
description: Encrypts whole files with AES-256 in Galois/Counter Mode, which provides both confidentiality and an authentication tag in one pass. Any tampering with the ciphertext is detected on decrypt, so a corrupted or maliciously altered file fails loudly instead of silently decrypting to garbage.

fields.side_channel_notes: use constant-time AES-NI; never reuse a nonce

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: XChaCha20-Poly1305 Messaging
description: Secures chat messages with the XChaCha20 stream cipher plus a Poly1305 authenticator, using a 192-bit nonce that can be chosen at random without collision risk. It needs no special hardware to run fast, which makes it ideal for phones and browsers doing end-to-end encrypted messaging.

fields.side_channel_notes: constant-time by design; safe random nonces

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: PBKDF2-SHA256 Key Derivation
description: Turns a human password into an encryption key by hashing it with a unique salt hundreds of thousands of times. The iteration count is deliberately expensive, so an attacker who steals the salted hash must pay that cost for every password guess, while the legitimate user pays it once.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Argon2id Password Hashing
description: Hashes passwords with Argon2id, the Password Hashing Competition winner, which is both memory-hard and side-channel resistant. Attackers with GPUs or custom chips gain little advantage because the algorithm forces large memory use per guess, leveling the field toward ordinary defenders.

fields.side_channel_notes: tune memory/time to ~0.5s on target hardware

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: AES Key Wrap (RFC 3394)
description: Wraps one encryption key inside another using the AES key-wrap construction, adding integrity so an unwrapping with the wrong key fails instead of producing a garbage key. It is the standard way to store data-encryption keys encrypted under a master key in key-management systems.

fields.side_channel_notes: constant-time unwrap; fail closed on integrity error

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Envelope Encryption
description: Encrypts data with a unique per-item data key, then encrypts that data key under a master key - the classic two-layer envelope. Data keys can be rotated or destroyed independently, and the master key never touches bulk data, which keeps the blast radius of any single key small.

fields.side_channel_notes: data key never persisted in clear

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: HMAC-SHA256 Integrity Tags
description: Attaches an HMAC-SHA256 tag computed with a secret key to every stored message, proving it was created by someone holding the key and never altered. Verification is a single hash comparison, making it the cheapest reliable integrity check for data at rest and in transit.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Secure Memory Wipe
description: Overwrites key material in RAM with zeros the moment it is no longer needed, using a wipe the compiler is not allowed to optimize away. Without this, keys linger in freed memory where a crash dump, swap file, or cold-boot attack could recover them long after use.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Encrypted Search (Blind Index)
description: Builds a blind index of keyed hashes over document keywords, letting a server find matching encrypted documents without ever seeing the keywords or the plaintext. The server learns only which documents match, which is the standard tradeoff that makes searchable encryption practical.

fields.side_channel_notes: fixed token length; pad result counts

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Forward-Secret Ratchet
description: Advances the encryption key with every message using a one-way ratchet, so compromising today's key reveals nothing about yesterday's messages. Old keys are deleted immediately after ratcheting, giving conversations forward secrecy even against future device theft.

fields.side_channel_notes: delete old keys at once; no key reuse

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Hardware-Bound Keys
description: Generates keys inside a hardware security module or secure enclave where the private material can never be exported. Operations happen inside the hardware boundary, so even a fully compromised operating system cannot steal the key - only ask the hardware to use it.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Encrypted Backups
description: Encrypts entire backups with a dedicated backup key before they leave the device, so cloud storage providers hold only ciphertext. The backup key itself is protected by the user's passphrase-derived key, keeping the whole chain under the user's control rather than the provider's.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Per-File Data Keys
description: Gives every file its own random data-encryption key instead of sharing one key across the vault. If one key is ever exposed, only one file is at risk, and individual files can be re-keyed or crypto-shredded without touching anything else.

fields.side_channel_notes: keys from CSPRNG; never derived from filename

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Side-Channel-Safe Comparison
description: Compares secrets like MAC tags and tokens in constant time, so the comparison duration reveals nothing about how many bytes matched. A naive early-exit comparison leaks the secret byte-by-byte to anyone who can measure response times precisely.

fields.side_channel_notes: no early exit; no data-dependent branches

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Crypto-Shredding Deletion
description: Deletes data by destroying its encryption key rather than overwriting every copy of the ciphertext. Since the key is small and centrally stored, deletion is instant and provable: without the key, all remaining ciphertext copies are permanently unreadable.

fields.side_channel_notes: destroy all key copies incl. backups

provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
